bottleneck: The first AAV dose reliably provokes humoral and T-cell responses that make re-dosing with the same vector virtually impossible: neutralizing antibodies intercept the vector and cytotoxic T-cells clear transduced cells. Because many gene therapies fade over years or miss enough cells on the first pass, the inability to give a second dose turns every treatment into a single irreversible attempt. Serotype switching helps only if the patient lacks cross-reactive immunity.
current_state: Re-dosing remains essentially unsolved in the clinic. Research focuses on engineered capsids that escape existing antibodies and on transient immunosuppression, with no established protocol.

sources.title: Addressing the Limitations of AAV Vectors through Evolutionary Guided Vector Design

title: AAV re-dosing blocked by post-treatment immunity
why_it_blocks: Without re-dosing there is no way to rescue partial responders or renew waning therapies, so dosing must be perfect the first time. This raises trial risk, narrows eligible patients, and freezes improvement of approved therapies.
